questions.q: What does RESTORE DATABASE actually do, as distinct from RECOVER DATABASE?
options: Copies datafiles from the backup back to disk — the database matches backup time, nothing more
Applies redo logs to bring the database to the current moment
Deletes obsolete backups per the retention policy
Opens the database for use immediately
questions.explain: RESTORE only puts files back; RECOVER is the separate step that applies redo on top of them.

options: Recovering all the way to the most recent possible point after a restore — the normal recovery case
Recovering to a deliberately earlier point in time using SET UNTIL TIME
Restoring a single tablespace instead of the whole database
Validating a backup without actually restoring it
questions.explain: Complete recovery replays all available redo to bring the database fully current after a restore.

questions.q: Why does incomplete recovery require ALTER DATABASE OPEN RESETLOGS instead of a plain OPEN?
options: Opening the database at a point in the past means the old redo log sequence no longer matches what actually happened afterward, so Oracle must start a new incarnation
RESETLOGS is only needed for tablespace-level restores
OPEN RESETLOGS is required for every RMAN restore, complete or incomplete
RESETLOGS re-encrypts the database after recovery
questions.explain: RESETLOGS marks a new incarnation because the redo stream diverges once the database opens in a state earlier than its true history.

questions.q: Why would a DBA restore and recover a single tablespace instead of the whole database?
options: It keeps the rest of the database online and serving traffic while only the affected tablespace is recovered
RMAN does not support whole-database restores
Tablespace-level restore is required before any whole-database restore
It's the only way to use block change tracking
questions.explain: A scoped tablespace restore limits the blast radius versus taking the entire instance offline.

questions.q: What does RESTORE DATABASE VALIDATE do?
options: Reads through backup pieces and checks for corruption without writing any files back
Restores the database to a temporary location for testing
Applies redo logs to validate they are intact
Registers the database with the recovery catalog
questions.explain: VALIDATE confirms a backup is actually usable without performing a real restore, a genuine way to test backups before an emergency.
